svg.title: Performance budget: measured values against the brief's targets
svg.desc: One row per budget row. Each bar is the measured value as a share of the brief's target, so the right-hand end of every track is the target itself: a bar that reaches it meets the row, a bar that stops short falls short, and a bar that would overrun it is clamped and labelled with its ratio. The 10,000-user row is drawn as a one-tenth bar: 1,000 simulated clients is what was actually driven through the ciphertext relay, which delivered every envelope with p95 12.2 ms. The chaos row is green because the relay was SIGKILLed mid-backlog and every one of its 20,000 accepted envelopes replayed from the log without loss - met for the single node that exists, not a fleet. The payload is re-measured from the current import graph; all other rows retain historical evidence under the recorded conditions in docs/LOAD_CHAOS.md and are not new audits, browser runs or device guarantees. The payload row is the cold load: the 119.9 KiB gzip module graph fetched on first panel open (M2, M3, M4, M9 SINGU AI, WebRTC/relay) is reported separately in LOAD_CHAOS.md rather than hidden inside the bar. The only row that reaches its full target and still falls short is the frame rate at maximum settings, two frames short, and it is labelled as such. The historical soak row is a full hour of samples whose minute-60 snapshot is smaller than the minute-10 snapshot; the per-minute heap after GC rose from 1.10 to 1.53 MiB. Columns are: row, value, and target.
svg.text: Measured value as a share of the brief's target
The right-hand end of each track is the target. Bars are clamped at the target; the ratio beside them is the real one.

SIGKILL: 20,000 replayed; failover: 20,000 re-posted, 0 lost - met
Current payload; other rows are historical recorded evidence, not new device guarantees. Relay: 1,000 clients, two local processes, not a fleet. See LOAD_CHAOS.md.
